# WastewaterSCAN national norovirus (GII) category for Oct 15, 2026: research notes (compiled Oct 5, 2026)

**Bottom line:** As of the last published data (through Sept 30, 2026), the national category is **LOW**, with a flat trend. Last year the national category went from Low to Medium at some point during October.

**Caveat on the resolution source:** the live dashboard at https://data.wastewaterscan.org/ only loads its data in a browser, so we could not read the current plotted value or its date. The national category below comes from WastewaterSCAN's monthly update posts (https://wwscan.ghost.io/). Someone needs to check the dashboard directly on Oct 15 or 16.

## 1. What the resolution source says

**Latest national category: LOW**
- Source: the September 2026 monthly update, posted Oct 2, 2026, covering data through Sept 30 (https://wwscan.ghost.io/nationwide-wastewaterscan-september-2026-update/).
- Exact quote: "Nationally, Norovirus is in the 'LOW' Wastewater Category with aggregated measurements showing low concentrations and no trend in the last 21 days."
- Median concentration was down less than 1% from August.
- Norovirus was detected in 99% of samples.

**Previous month: LOW**
- The August 2026 update, posted Sept 2, 2026 (https://wwscan.ghost.io/nationwide-wastewaterscan-august-2026-update/), said LOW with no trend.
- Median concentration was down about 12% from July.
- MedicalDaily repeated this on Sept 21, 2026 (https://www.medicaldaily.com/norovirus-season-florida-fall-2026-low-levels-now-478902).

**How the category is calculated — this matters for the question**
- WastewaterSCAN's published category is not just the concentration compared with the past 365 days, as the question's wording implies. It combines three things (per https://data.wastewaterscan.org/about/ and the monthly updates):
  - the concentration compared with national thirds (the 33rd and 67th percentiles) of all sites' data over the past 365 days;
  - the trend over the last 21 days;
  - how often the virus is detected.
- Norovirus is treated as a "commonly detected" pathogen.
- The exact rule for combining these three is not published (uncertain).
- **Precedent where the trend raised the category:** the September 2024 update, published Oct 4, 2024, rated the nation HIGH even though concentrations were only "medium," because of a "significant upward trend over the last 3 weeks" (https://wwscan.ghost.io/nationwide-wwscan-september-2024-update/).
- The question resolves on whatever category the dashboard displays, so this combined method is what actually decides it.

## 2. Recent news, current status and upcoming events

**The 2025–26 season was long, so the 365-day comparison window has a high baseline.** The window ending Oct 15, 2026 includes this whole season, which probably raises the bar for Medium or High on concentration alone (our inference).

**CDC NoroSTAT outbreak counts (page updated Sept 17, 2026)** (https://www.cdc.gov/norovirus/php/reporting/norostat-data.html)
- 27 outbreaks from Aug 1 to Sept 4, 2026, compared with 29 in the same period of 2025.
- That is within the normal range for 2012–2026.

**Local signals**
- Around Sept 30, 2026, a Yahoo/Idaho Statesman article reported Boise-area wastewater at "high" and rising for at least 21 days. This was not read directly and is only one local area.
- No mainstream coverage in August–October 2026 reported an early national rise or a new variant.

**Program operations**
- WastewaterSCAN is still running (Stanford/Emory, with Verily as the lab, funded by the Sergey Brin Family Foundation; https://www.wastewaterscan.org/about). The Sept 2026 update came out on schedule on Oct 2.
- We found no announcement that the program is shutting down.
- A separate CDC sampling network (NWSS) had a Verily contract gap: the old contract ran through Sept 14, 2026, a new one was awarded Sept 28, 2026, and about 200 CDC sites briefly lost data (https://www.inkl.com/news/about-200-cdc-wastewater-sites-will-briefly-lose-data-and-the-agency-has-given-no-start-date). It is unclear whether this affects WastewaterSCAN.

**Scheduled events before Oct 15**
- None known. The October 2026 monthly update will come out around early November, after the resolution date.
- The dashboard itself updates continuously (several samples per week per site), and data usually lags by a few days.

## 3. Base rates: the national category in mid-October in past years

| Year | Evidence | Mid-October category |
|---|---|---|
| 2025 | Sept update (posted Oct 6, 2025): LOW, no trend, but median already up about 16% from August (https://wwscan.ghost.io/nationwide-wastewaterscan-september-2025-update/). Oct update (posted Nov 3, 2025): MEDIUM, no trend; sites 72 Low / 44 Medium / 19 High; the South rising since mid-September (https://wwscan.ghost.io/nationwide-wastewaterscan-october-2025-update/) | Low or Medium; exact switch date unknown |
| 2024 (GII.17 season) | HIGH as of Sept 30, 2024, driven by the trend. WastewaterSCAN later said levels "started to increase in early October 2024 and peaked early February 2025" | Probably HIGH; no October 2024 update was found, so this is inferred |
| 2023 | National HIGH by Nov 22, 2023; median went from 2.8M copies/g in October to 3.94M (https://wwscan.ghost.io/nationwide-wwscan-update-11-22-23/). California sites were mostly in the lower third on Oct 25, 2023 | Unknown, probably Low or Medium |
| 2022 | No data found; the category system may not have existed yet (unverified) | Unknown |

**Typical seasonal curve**
- Low through August and September.
- Rises from early or mid October, often starting in the South or Midwest.
- High by mid-to-late November.
- Peaks between December and February.
- Stays high into March through May.

**Comparison with 2025:** at the end of September 2026, concentrations were flat (down less than 1% month over month). At the same point in 2025 they were already up 16% month over month.

## Key uncertainties
- We could not read the live dashboard's current category or the date of its latest data point.
- The rule combining concentration, trend and detection frequency is not published. A significant 21-day upward trend could lift the category even when concentrations are low or medium (as in Sept 2024).
- We could not pin down the exact date the category switched in October 2025.

WastewaterSCAN assigns one of three categories — "Low", "Medium", or "High" — to its national Norovirus (GII) overview by comparing current national concentrations to the prior 365 days across all participating sites. The question resolves to whichever of the three options matches the category that the dashboard displays as the national Norovirus (GII) level for the most recent available data point dated on or before October 15, 2026, as observed on the dashboard on October 15 or October 16, 2026. If the dashboard shows a plotted national Norovirus value specifically for October 15, 2026, that point's category governs; otherwise the category of the latest plotted point dated on or before October 15, 2026 governs. Later revisions to the dashboard after October 16, 2026 do not change resolution.

A late dashboard update is not grounds for annulment; if no data point dated on or before October 15, 2026 has posted by October 16, 2026, resolution waits until the relevant data point is finalized.

(b) **Status quo:** "Low." The September 2026 update, covering data through September 30, put the nation at LOW with no 21-day trend. Median concentration was down less than 1% from August. The question background says some early-October reporting showed "Medium." That conflicts with the dashboard snapshot showing "Low," which suggests values sit near the Low/Medium boundary.

(c) **Base rates:**
- **2025:** Low at the end of September, Medium by the end of October. The switch came sometime in October, and concentrations had already risen 16% month over month by end of September.
- **2024:** High by September 30, lifted by a strong upward trend in a GII.17 season.
- **2023:** Probably Low or Medium in mid-October.

The seasonal rise typically starts in early to mid October. Two factors favor staying Low:
- This year was flat at end of September, unlike 2025.
- The 365-day comparison window includes a long, high 2025–26 season, which raises the concentration bar for Medium.

Against that, values are near the boundary, the seasonal rise is imminent, and a local signal (Boise) is rising. If a significant 21-day upward trend develops, the combined rating method can push the category up a level.

(d) **Unexpected scenario:** an early, steep national rise driven by the South or Midwest, possibly from a new variant, creates a significant 21-day upward trend by mid-October. Combined with Medium-level concentrations, that could produce a "High" rating, as in September 2024. Alternatively, a brief dip or noise keeps the category firmly Low despite the season.
